title: Lemme just dip my toes in over here
author: obake84
selftext:
ok this is gonna be my first post on this.

Im building a game using ai pipelines, there I said it.

and no AI didnt fucking write this. Im typing this shit out off the dome. Deal with it, errors and all. Which is actually kind of the point here, I dont want AI to be creative, that shits been bouncing around upstairs for a while but I want to see if I can use it to actually build the damn thing.

Ive always wanted to be a creative person. Im in a software QA role and am a life long nerd and gamer. Ive dabbled in some OO languages such as ruby when I was in one job and java in another plus QA knowledge acquired over 13 years in the biz.

I have always had ideas but never had the time to learn coding to bring it to life. I know how software is developed and shipped to production but never done it myself. Basically I know all the boring stuff that has to happen Ive just never been the dude actually making the whole thing.

Then along came a tool at work I used called amazon q and it was a game changer, then a conference, then another light bulb moment (insert gif of that guy with the hair and the explosion around his head for something mind blowing) and then one called writer and then chatGPT then copilot and codex etc etc you get the point now.

I dabbled, did silly prompts and such then went to another conference and had that (insert gif image in your head again but 10x) and then came home and got to work on a side project. I drank the 100 dollar koolaid for chatGPT and a shot of claude at 20 bucks. In fact, Im hoping to release soon once I clean up the redteam AI slop I have ( cant be one of those "vibecoders" now can I)

My brain connecting the dots I figured why not just treat this like pieces of an actual software team.

Now Ive taken all of that and blasted it into a full ass SDLC team to take a stab at being one of those "I made a game in 48 hours" people but like actually deliver something dope af without skipping all the boring shit that makes software not suck and maybe just maybe make my muse happy by finally getting one idea out the door.

Im talking product, analyst, arc, dev, qa, release, redteam, the whole shebang. Not because I want to cosplay as a FANG (or whatever those diamond hand folks call it these days) but because Ive spent 13 years living what happens when you skip that shit. So thats it really, can one person use AI to leverage the team without throwing away all the boring engineering shit that keeps software from sucking?

So, now that I have rambled. I want to start a youtube channel to deep dive into my process (none of that faceless crap either, you see my ugly mug and like it) and you can read my posts here which will have a journal of my journey. (also built by AI workflows so slap me with AI slop if its there, I can take it, my body is ready)

And not just the good stuff the not so good too. The prompts that didnt work, agents going off the deep end (fucking claude), QA finding stuff, me realizing this doesnt work or maybe it does, all of it.

Anywho, you have read this much so here we go, buckle up.

The idea is a game! Haha shocker, Im not sure Im ready to give the deets yet for those scummy copy cats so the repo will be private until I have my proverbial "demo" ready. Some inspirations, balatro, slay the spire, deadcells, dicey dungeons, astrea: six-sided oracles roguelite/roguelike (fuck if I can tell the difference sometimes) but its a play on words for the name and its hopefully got a tight (toiht like a tiger) gameplay loop. Its called Pair a Dice and the basic idea is you're trying to make it to an island paradise with a pair of dice, except I'm playing around with different polyhedral dice instead of just making everything d6s.

Thats about as much as Im giving away for now because Id like to at least be the first person to make my own bad version of it.

So, if you liked this and wanna know more stay tuned and slap me with feedback please, I need it! (especially if you think Im disappearing up my own ass with this AI stuff then for real tell me).

comments.body:
Ill just get in front of the stack question:  
  
Godot 4.7.2 + GDScript for the game, Git, SQLite for project/workflow memory, and AI-assisted pixel art/sprite generation for the visual side. ChatGPT/Codex/Claude are doing different jobs around the SDLC. Nothing super exotic — the weird part is how I've wired the process together.
